decisions.27.159: Cannan II line 5271: assemblies can ever, not can never, matching argument; modern EN already right.
decisions.27.187: Cannan II line 5896: most convenient for that part [of the capital], not port.
decisions.31.10: II lines 13508–12: extraordinary assistance, not ordinary.
decisions.31.12: II lines 13535–36: forfeiture of the funds of its creditor (not credit).
decisions.31.136: II line 15585 confirms Smith writes one eighth; preserved and annotated in both languages. With net 1 and 10% tax, gross = 10/9, hence a 1/9 raise.
decisions.31.178: II line 16237: wool-fells, sheepskins with the wool, not felts. Existing modern EN correct.
decisions.31.184: II lines 16355–60 distinguish two motivations and the alternatives of obtaining an export bounty or a drawback; damaged original and conflated modern EN corrected.
decisions.11.105: Smith says 1262 and 51 Henry III, Cannan I line 8921. Regnal year began in 1266. Both versions distinguish Smith’s statement from the editorial note. Historical statute text: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Statutes_at_Large_(Ruffhead)/Volume_1/Judic._Pillorie_(51_Hen3._Stat_6)_(1266).
decisions.11.182: mints, not mines: Cannan vol I local text line 10214. Existing modern English already correct; Danish now explicitly møntsteder.
decisions.11.203: Cannan vol I lines 10634–35: understocked relative to complete cultivation, but overstocked relative to actual produce. Original and retained modern English incorrectly had overstocked both times; corrected first occurrence in candidate English.
decisions.11.223: Cannan vol I lines 11081–85 preserves author arithmetic discrepancy: 12s/(6s8d per 8 bushels)=14.4 bushels, not14.8; times3s6d=50s4.8d, divided5 hides=10s0.96d. Author figures retained with separately labelled bilingual editorial note.
decisions.11.239: Author inverse-proportion arithmetic preserved and separately explained bilingually. Cannan I11424–27 repeats source thirds/fourths/fifths. Correct inverse rises are1/2,1/3,1/4 for respective value falls1/3,1/4,1/5.
